items.question: How does the yogin perform continuous inner worship of the deity?
premises: The yogin makes the support-ground washed by a moment of sprinkling with the essence of wonder.
The yogin offers flowers of innate nature taken from the mind, bearing their own fragrance.
The offering proceeds by the method of the priceless vessel of one's own heart full of bliss-nectar.
The worship takes place in the temple of the body together with the goddess.
items.inference: Therefore the yogin worships the deity day and night through an internalized ritual using the body's own faculties and states.
uncertainties: The exact parsing of devārcaye as a denominative or compound verb is interpretive but does not affect the sense.
items.plain_english: Having made the support-ground cleansed by a moment of sprinkling with the essence of wonder, I worship you, O God, together with the Goddess day and night in the temple of the body, using flowers of my own nature taken from the mind and filled with their own fragrance, through the method of the priceless offering-vessel of my own heart overflowing with the nectar of bliss.

items.question: What manifests when one abides anywhere in one's own reflective awareness?
premises: One may stand anywhere in this manner.
Such standing is by the nature of one's own reflective awareness.
In that very place the entry of the three powers occurs.
items.inference: Therefore the entry of the three powers shines forth threefold wherever one abides in one's own reflective awareness.
items.plain_english: Thus, wherever one may stand, by the very nature of one's own reflective awareness, there the entry of the three powers shines forth in a threefold way.

items.question: How does the threefold shining expand into a fuller state of repose?
premises: This arises from the stated twelve wheels.
The repose occurs in a single moment.
items.inference: Therefore the repose of that ninefold shining, arising from the twelve wheels, occurs in a single moment and has a state of one hundred and eight.
items.plain_english: When that shining appears ninefold, arising from the stated twelve wheels, its repose occurs in a single moment and takes the form of a state numbering one hundred and eight.

items.question: How is the yogin's speech understood in relation to this unified state?
premises: That state is clearly discerned as one alone, numbering a hundred.
In this way the yogin's expression arises within that state.
Whatever speech of this yogin may occur is included in that discernment.
items.inference: Therefore any speech whatsoever of the yogin is understood as belonging to that single unified state.
uncertainties: The compound kiṃcanaitasya is taken as kiṃcana + etasya; the fused surface is preserved as one token.
items.plain_english: That state is clearly discerned as one alone, numbering a hundred; and in this way, whatever speech at all may arise from this yogin belongs to that same state.

items.question: How does the yogin's speech function as mantra practice on the unsurpassed path?
premises: Whatever speech arises from the yogin belongs to the unified state.
That speech becomes mantra practice on the unsurpassed path.
This occurs constantly without depending on the presence of inner fuel.
items.inference: Therefore the yogin's speech itself becomes continuous mantra practice on the unsurpassed path without requiring any inner fuel.
items.plain_english: That very speech becomes mantra practice on the unsurpassed path, constantly and without any need to rely on the presence of inner fuel.

items.question: What happens when all beings are understood to enter that blazing awareness?
premises: A fire blazes with hundreds of front flames spreading from all the masses of senses.
All beings may be considered to enter there.
This entry is presented as a matter of reflective understanding.
items.inference: Therefore, if the entry of all beings into that blazing awareness is reflectively understood, that very locus is the site of universal absorption.
items.plain_english: If one reflectively understands that all beings enter into that which blazes with hundreds of foremost flames spreading forth from all the streams of the senses, then that very place is where their entry occurs.
